newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY LEAGUE-MANLY BEAT CRONULLA TO REACH ARL FINAL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-MANLY BEAT CRONULLA TO REACH ARL FINAL.

text.p: Manly on Sunday scored four unanswered tries to trounce Cronulla 24-0 in an Australian Rugby League (ARL) premiership semifinal and reach next week's grand final against St George.
St George upset North Sydney 29-12 onm Saturday to book an unexpected berth in the grand final.
A methodical Manly lived up to the form which saw them comfortably top the ARL standings at the end of regular season matches and they completely outclassed the young Cronulla side.
The only black note for Manly was a head injury suffered by New Zealand fullback Matthew Ridge early in the match.
Ridge was taken from the field unconscious on a motorised stretcher 25 minutes into the match after attempting a tackle on Cronulla centre Paul Donaghy
Manly medical staff later told reporters Ridge had been badly concussed after being hit in the head by Donaghy's knee.
The fitness of Ridge will now be one of Manly's primary concerns in the leadup to next Sunday's grand final.
Ridge had kicked a penalty goal in the 10th minute and had a hand in his side's first try, scored by veteran standoff Cliff Lyons, as Manly set up a 6-0 halftime lead.

The second half started badly for Cronulla when fullback David Peachey dropped the ball in a tackle in only the first minute, allowing Manly secondrower Steve Menzies to cross for his side's second try.
Another Peachey error 18 minutes later, this time from a high kick by Lyons, led to a try by winger Danny Moore.
Menzies then crossed for his second try six minutes from fulltime to give Manly an unbeatable lead.
St George's had been ranked 100-1 outsiders at the start of the season when coach Rod Reddy and a number of key players left and the club considered a merger because of financial troubles.
Manly and St George have played in two previous grand finals, in 1957 and 1959, with St George winning both times.
